📝Coalition on Paper📝
In reality, the Houthis hold the initiative

Houthi attacks in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait have resulted in new costs for countries actively using the Red Sea for their cargo and resource supplies. Saudi Arabia suffered particularly.

And now the Saudis, if Reuters is to be believed, are working to create an international coalition to protect shipping in the Red Sea from Houthi attacks. The composition of the possible structure has yet to be determined, and talks are underway with dozens of countries.

🖍The kingdom's interests amid everything happening in the Middle East are understandable. First came the war in the Persian Gulf, which forced a reorientation of exports to the Red Sea shores, and now a resumption of clashes with the Houthis.

However, returning to the same experience of confrontation in the Strait of Hormuz, the Americans tried to do the same thing—create a coalition where they would lead while others did the dirty work. And what came of it?

❗️There were no takers whatsoever (given all the risks, this makes sense). And with Yemen, things look roughly the same – the only difference is a smaller arsenal compared to the Iranians. Therefore, the Saudi idea will clearly not cause much excitement, but unlike the Iranian shores, the probability of the idea being realized in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait is somewhat higher.
